subject: Economics
title: Forward vertical integration: pros and cons

stages.name: Forward vertical integration: pros and cons
stages.title: Forward vertical integration: pros and cons
stages.sub: The student can explain the main advantages and disadvantages of a manufacturer buying a retailer.

steps.q: A tea manufacturer used to sell its tea to an independent retailer, who then sold it to customers in its own shops. Now the manufacturer buys that retailer outright. Whose shops are they now?
steps.hint: Buying a business means taking ownership of it.

steps.q: If a rival's tea only reaches shelves because a shop owner agrees to stock it, and the manufacturer now owns the shop, who decides whether the manufacturer's own tea gets shelf space?
steps.hint: The manufacturer now owns the shops that reach customers.
steps.pre: Owning the outlet gives the manufacturer

steps.q: The manufacturer has spent 20 years making tea, but has never run a shop: staffing tills, managing store layouts, handling retail returns. On day one of running its new shops, is it likely to run them as smoothly as an experienced retailer would?
steps.right: No, it will probably struggle at first
steps.wrong: Yes, running a shop is much the same as making tea
steps.hint: Making a product and selling it face-to-face to customers are different skills.

steps.q: Before the takeover, the manufacturer sold tea to the retailer for £2 a box, and the retailer sold it on to customers for £3 a box, keeping the £1 difference. Now that the manufacturer owns the shop, who keeps that £1 when a box is sold?
steps.right: The manufacturer, since it now owns the shop
steps.wrong: No one, the £1 disappears once they merge
steps.hint: The retailer's old profit on each box has to go somewhere once the manufacturer owns the shop too.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: Now that it owns the shops, the manufacturer can choose the shop layout, staff training and the way tea is displayed and presented to customers. Before the takeover, could it decide any of that?
steps.right: No, the independent retailer decided it
steps.hint: Before the takeover, the shop belonged to someone else.

steps.q: Buying an entire chain of shops, then merging its staff, systems and stock into the manufacturer's business, costs a lot of money and can go wrong. Is this a small, easily reversed step for the manufacturer?
steps.right: No, it is expensive and risky
steps.wrong: Yes, it is a cheap and simple step
steps.hint: Think about the price of buying an entire chain of shops, plus the risk of the merger failing.
